patches.title: Lighting
patches.description: Fast uses the game's own non-tiled lighting renderer and skips the tiled-lighting compute passes (about 17% shorter frames on the world map; neon outline glow is slightly dimmer).

sites.note: lighting stage selection, function 0x73eb850 (guest 0x77eb850): 'test r14b,r14b; je' -> always the non-tiled renderer

patches.title: Upscaling
patches.description: Renders the 3D scene at 720p or 900p instead of 1080p and lets Apple MetalFX (spatial) scale it to the game's output size; menus and text stay sharp. Fewer pixels to shade: shorter frames. Off is the game's own 1080p picture and upscaler (NPS5_ASTRO_UPSCALING=off). The default is MetalFX 720p. 720p and 900p set the renderer's light-tile grid fix (KYTY_ASTRO_TILE_GRID=auto) that removes the blocky squares on dust, glass and particles; spatial MetalFX has no anti-aliasing of its own, so edges can look more jagged than Off. Needs a Mac with MetalFX (macOS 13+); the dynamic-resolution lock of the standard build is assumed.

sites.note: scene parameters, dynamic-resolution level 0 case of function 0x73be670 (guest 0x77be670): 'vmovss xmm0, [rip+0xf9151e]' loads the level width as a float (texture LOD bias)
same case: 'movabs rdx, 0x43800000780' = the level's {width, height} pair
scene parameters, dynamic-resolution level 0 case of function 0x70cef60 (guest 0x74cef60): 'vmovd xmm0, [rip+0x127fba8]' loads the level width as a float (texture LOD bias)
same case: 'movabs rcx, 0x43800000780' = the level's {width, height} pair

patches.title: Render scale
patches.description: Automatic: the 3D scene renders at 720p and drops to 540p while frames take longer than the budget (33 ms = 30 fps; NPS5_RENDER_TARGET_MS), back to 720p when there is headroom; MetalFX upscales either size, menus and text stay sharp. 540p gives about 6 % shorter frames on an M4 Pro (Sky Garden) for a softer picture. The switch uses the game's own dynamic-resolution pipeline sets (level 1 is built at 960x540), so nothing is re-created. NPS5_RENDER=auto|720|540 chooses too, NPS5_RENDER_LEVELS sets it per level; 720p is the game as before. Assumes the Upscaling setting's 720p.

per-frame application update, function 0xc53370 (guest 0x1053370): 'mov eax, [rax+0x2fae30]' = the renderer's requested DRS level; the game compares it with the current level and switches pipeline sets [app+0x15c0+8*level] on a change
same selector, other branch: 'mov eax, [rbx+0x2390]' = the application's DRS level
per-frame scene level getter, function 0x7418ad0 (guest 0x7818ad0): 'mov eax, ebx' returns the scene's DRS level (read only by the light-tile grid table lookup); a negative level (no DRS) stays
